record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.original_question: For liquids and other many-body systems whose nonequilibrium description requires two-particle density matrices rather than only single-particle quasiparticle operators, how can one obtain a usable closure condition for the nonequilibrium thermodynamic description when the two-particle potential couples reduced density matrices of all orders into a BBGKY-like hierarchy?

evidence.quote: This is not the case for liquids, when two-particle density matrices are required to be added to the description.

But in this case a closure condition cannot be obtained since the two-particle potential, which differently to Coulomb interaction in solids, cannot be dealt with in a molecular field approximation, couples the reduced density matrices of all order leading to a kind of BBGKY hierarchy in nonequilibrium conditions requiring the introduction at a certain point of a decoupling approximation like in the theory of Green functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a classical or quantum many-body system (for instance a dense liquid) interacting via a pairwise two-body potential V(r_i, r_j) that cannot be approximated by a mean (molecular) field. Let \rho_s(1,...,s; t) denote the s-particle reduced density matrices (or distribution functions) obtained by partial trace from the full N-body nonequilibrium statistical operator \rho_N(t). Their evolution equations form a BBGKY-like hierarchy in which the equation for \rho_s involves \rho_{s+1} through the two-body potential, so that all orders of reduced density matrices are coupled.

Suppose one wishes to construct a nonequilibrium thermodynamic description of such a system in the framework of a maximum-entropy nonequilibrium statistical ensemble formalism, where the chosen basic dynamical variables include not only the one-particle (quasiparticle) density operator but also the two-particle density matrix \rho_2.

Problem. Provide an explicit and physically justified closure condition for this hierarchy at the level of the two-particle reduced density matrix \rho_2, that is, a prescription expressing \rho_3 (and hence implicitly all higher \rho_s) as a functional of \rho_1 and \rho_2, such that:

(i) the resulting closed system of evolution equations for \rho_1 and \rho_2 is consistent with the maximum-entropy / informational-statistical structure (i.e., it preserves positivity, normalization, and the H-theorem-type entropy production properties of the underlying ensemble);

(ii) it reduces, in appropriate limits (dilute gas, weak coupling, equilibrium), to known and validated approximations such as the Boltzmann, Vlasov, or equilibrium Kirkwood / Born–Green–Yvon closures;

(iii) it yields a usable, computationally tractable nonequilibrium thermodynamic description for liquids with strong short-range two-body interactions for which a molecular-field decoupling is inapplicable.

Determine such a closure, or prove that no closure satisfying (i)–(iii) can exist within this framework.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of obtaining a principled, generally valid closure of the BBGKY hierarchy at the two-particle level for strongly interacting liquids in nonequilibrium conditions remains an unresolved foundational problem in nonequilibrium statistical mechanics. Available approaches (Kirkwood superposition, mode-coupling, Green-function decouplings, density-functional closures) are approximate and regime-dependent; no universally accepted closure compatible with a maximum-entropy nonequilibrium ensemble formalism has been established. No definitive resolution was located in the literature.

status_evidence.title: BBGKY hierarchy - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Closing the BBGKY hierarchy requires approximations; common ones include the Boltzmann, Vlasov, and Kirkwood superposition closures, none of which is exact for dense, strongly interacting liquids.
status_evidence.claim: No exact general closure of the BBGKY hierarchy is known; available closures are approximations valid only in specific regimes.
